title: Prevent transient DNS misbinds from stale NAT mappings during peering rehome
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Multiple customers reported transient incorrect DNS resolution following automated VPC peering rehome operations on Dedicated nodes. Symptoms included tenant A resolving tenant B hostnames for 10-30s after peering reassignment during scale events. This ticket tracks detection, a safe hotfix, and a longer-term reconciliation/autorepair for stale NAT and resolver affinity state that leads to DNS misbinds.
reproduction_steps: Trigger dedicated capacity scale-down that moves tenant allocation between peered nodes (simulate peering rehome).
From an external client inside the tenant VPC, continuously resolve a stable internal hostname belonging to tenant A while peering switch occurs.
Observe transient resolution returning an IP owned by tenant B for 10-30s correlated with SNAT/NAT reallocation events on the egress nodes.
Check conntrack/SNAT tables and resolver affinity entries on both source and destination nodes to see stale mappings.
Note that impacted requests still have correct TLS session metadata (SNI) but DNS answer maps to wrong tenant IP.
Replay with increased concurrency and observe probability of misbind increases when ephemeral NAT pools are exhausted.
root_cause: A race between peering reassignment and the ephemeral NAT allocator plus delayed resolver affinity reconciliation. When a tenant's egress mapping moves, conntrack entries and per-node resolver affinity entries can persist briefly. If the ephemeral NAT pool reuses ports/IPs rapidly, a different tenant can get the same 5-tuple mapping before resolver affinity updates propagate, causing DNS answers to map to the wrong tenant's IP until cache/conntrack TTLs expire.
mitigation_steps: Immediate: deploy a conservative heuristic to delay NAT port reuse for 60s after peering rehome for affected tenant IP ranges (hotpatch to allocator service).
Hotfix: ensure egress controller clears resolver-affinity cache entries for tenants undergoing reassignment and emits an explicit DNS-invalidated event to console metrics.
Workaround for customers: suggest enabling dedicated-egress-reserve flag to prefer tenant-specific ephemeral ranges during noisy scales until fix is live.
Communication: notify impacted customers via support channel with timeline and temporary mitigation steps.
rollout_plan: Stage 0: Merge unit and integration tests into main branch (complete).
Stage 1: Canary deploy hotfix to two non-production Dedicated clusters in us-west-2 (2 hours, monitor).
Stage 2: Roll to 25% of Dedicated fleet for customers flagged as low-risk (24 hours).
Stage 3: Full fleet rollout with traffic shaping and rollback window (48 hours).
Rollback criteria: spike in 5xx errors, >0.1% increase in per-tenant DNS mismatch alerts, or significant latency regressions.
testing_plan: Unit tests for allocator to assert no reuse inside hold-window semantics.
Integration test simulating peering rehome with mocked conntrack and ensuring no DNS misbinds across 1k resolution attempts.
Chaos test: run node drain + immediate reattach with heavy ephemeral NAT churn and assert no cross-tenant resolution.
Manual validation with impacted customer's VPC under support supervision.
notes: Design decision: prefer a short hold-window (60s) instead of longer TTLs to minimize cost/perf impact; revisit after telemetry stabilizes.
We considered adding strong serializable locks across allocator and controlplane but rejected for now due to outage blast radius and latency impact.
Security review: this hotfix does not change cryptographic handling; KMS/HSM unaffected.
Follow-up: schedule a refactor to tag ephemeral SNAT allocations with tenant-ownership tokens to enable deterministic reclamation.
Customer support: CS has draft message and will send targeted updates to three impacted customers once canary passes.
